metadata.title: Cooper Rush - Inactive, available as emergency QB
metadata.description: Rush (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game versus Green Bay.
metadata.analysis: Rush started for Atlanta in the team's first two games of the 2026 campaign. However, the signal-caller struggled overall, throwing for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions while completing just 56.4 percent of his attempts. With Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) back in the equation, Rush will be inactive against the Packers, though he will be available in an emergency situation.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush emergency 3rd QB for Thursday
metadata.description: Cooper Rush will be the Falcons' emergency third QB for their game against the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Rush was awful in his chances as a starter through two weeks, so heaven forbid he see his name called up again.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush abysmal in loss to Panthers
metadata.description: Cooper Rush completed 10 of 17 passes for 86 yards with two picks in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also ran twice for 20 yards and lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: It was an abysmal showing for Rush, who was benched halfway through for Jack Strand, who wasn't much, if any, better. Michael Penix is rumored to return to the lineup for Thursday's game, but if he doesn't, it's not worth starting any Falcon aside from Bijan Robinson.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush - Benched after rough showing
metadata.description: Rush completed 10 of 17 passes for 86 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing twice for 20 yards before being benched in the third quarter of the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Rush's afternoon was about as difficult as his numbers suggest, and after he tossed his second interception of the day with 7:13 remaining in the third quarter, the veteran quarterback's day was done. Rookie replacement Jack Strand wasn't any better and tossed a pick-six during his time in the game, but if either Michael Penix (knee) or Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is able to suit up for Thursday's Week 3 road matchup against the Packers, Rush may not necessarily be a shoo-in for No. 2 quarterback duties over his first-year teammate.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush a Very Low-End Option at QB in Week 2
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush didn't do much with his opportunity as starting QB in Week 1's loss to Pittsburgh, completing 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards and one touchdown while tossing two interceptions. The veteran QB will get another shot in Week 2 against a much softer defense as the Falcons take on the Panthers at home. Last week, Caleb Williams threw for 269 yards and two scores while adding 10 rushes for 65 yards and an additional two touchdowns. Rush is not the same caliber of quarterback as Williams, though, and with the Bears running at will against Carolina (two running backs had over 100 yards), the Falcons could very well try to do the same thing with Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. With a likely heavy dose of the ground attack and a low likelihood of being very effective through the air, the nine-year pro ranks as QB31 this week at RotoBaller, making him avoidable outside of Superflex leagues and sets him up as a DFS dart throw in tournaments.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush - Announced as Week 2 starter
metadata.description: Coach Kevin Stefanski said Friday that Rush will start Sunday's contest against the Panthers, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
metadata.analysis: At the same time, Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) was deemed doubtful to play, and Michael Penix (knee) was ruled out for Week 2 action, per Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site. Rush got the Week 1 nod under center with both Tagovailoa and Penix sidelined, but he didn't fare too well through the air, completing 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while getting sacked four times.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush (back) expected to start behind center in Week 2
metadata.description: Cooper Rush (back) is expected to start at quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2 according to Ian Rapoport.
metadata.analysis: Rush continues to fight through a back issue that popped up for head coach Kevin Stefanski, but barring any setbacks is poised to start behind center with Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) still sidelined. The quarterback underwhelmed in a Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers and should not be considered starter-worthy against the Carolina Panthers Sunday.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush - Expected to start Week 2
metadata.description: Rush is expected to start Week 2 against Carolina after taking the Falcons' first-team reps Friday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Tua Tagovailoa (back) hasn't practiced this week, and Michael Penix (knee) apparently isn't ready to play. Rush completed just 12 of 22 pass attempts in Sunday's 20-13 loss at Pittsburgh despite sending 10 of those passes to RB Bijan Robinson, who accounted for 65.8 percent of the team's yards from scrimmage.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush Confirmed as Week 2 Starter
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush has again been named the starter ahead of the team's Week 2 divisional matchup with the Carolina Panthers, with head coach Kevin Stefanski confirming on Friday. Rush was thrust into a starting role two days ahead of the Falcons' season-opening loss to the Steelers, when Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) popped up on the injury report and was ruled out with an oblique injury. With the Falcons already ruling out 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. ahead of Sunday's game, Rush will make his second consecutive start, making all Falcons pass-catchers difficult to trust even against a Panthers defense fresh off allowing 59 points to the Chicago Bears. Rush completed only 12 passes in Week 1, with eight going to running back Bijan Robinson, while Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. combined for four targets, two receptions, and 29 yards. Rush is RotoBaller's QB32 for Week 2.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush Trending Towards Making Another Start
metadata.description: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Cooper Rush is taking the majority of the throws with the starters in the final practice of the week on Friday, according to Marc Raimondi of ESPN. Raimondi notes that this is the same way last Friday looked before Rush made the start in the Week 1 season-opening loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Michael Penix Jr. (knee) has been practicing in full as he finishes off the final stages of his recovery from a partially torn ACL late last year, but without full first-team reps in practice this week, he is unlikely to make his 2026 season debut this weekend against the division-rival Carolina Panthers. Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) has not practiced all week and is expected to be officially ruled out for Week 2 on Friday. The 32-year-old Rush threw for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in last week's 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he could be in for a better showing this weekend against a Carolina defense that gave up nearly 60 points to the Chicago Bears in the season opener.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush (back) logs full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Cooper Rush (back) officially logged a full practice session on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran quarterback was able to log another full practice session on Thursday and should be fully good to go for Week 2. It's still unclear who will be Atlanta's starting quarterback on Sunday, but it looks like it's between Rush and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) at this point with Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) still not back at practice.

metadata.title: Cooper Rush (back) practicing with starters Thursday
metadata.description: Cooper Rush (back) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) were both throwing passes with Atlanta's starters on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Rush was the starter for Atlanta in Week 1, and with Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) still not practicing, it looks like the starting nod in Week 2 will be between him and Michael Penix Jr. (knee). They were both practicing with the starters on Thursday, so it seems like the team has yet to make a decision on who will be at the helm for them against the Panthers this week.
